claims.claim_text: Can't Stop analysis: four dice flatten odds, middle columns dominate, consistent probabilistic strategies win, design favors playability.
claims.evidence_quote: Four-dice probabilities flatten the distribution ... Probabilistic strategies dominate ... Perfect balance isn't necessary
claims.reasoning: All summary strands (flattened odds, middle-column dominance, probabilistic winners, playability) appear in source conclusion.

claims.claim_text: Roll four dice, pair freely, advance three active markers; bust loses the turn's progress.
claims.evidence_quote: roll four dice, pair them up however you want ... if you can't move any of your three active markers, you lose everything you've gained that turn
claims.reasoning: Source states exactly this rule set.

claims.claim_text: Columns 2-12 have lengths 3-5-7-9-11-13-11-9-7-5-3; complete three columns to win.
claims.evidence_quote: 2 and 12: 3 steps ... 7: 13 steps. You need to complete three columns to win
claims.reasoning: Sequence matches the source column lengths and win condition.

claims.claim_text: Forced-move rule: chosen pairing forces ALL its legal moves, even unwanted ones.
claims.evidence_quote: you must take all available moves ... you must make ALL legal moves from that pairing, even if you don't want them
claims.reasoning: Direct restatement of the forced-move rule.

claims.claim_text: (1,1,3,4) as 2+7 on {6,7,8} forces taking both 2 and 7.
claims.evidence_quote: you roll (1,1,3,4) ... pairing (1,1)+(3,4) = 2+7 ... forced to take BOTH the 2 and the 7
claims.reasoning: Source example matches numbers and forced outcome.

claims.claim_text: Two-dice baseline peaks at 7 with 16.67%, exactly 6x likelier than 2 at 2.78%.
claims.evidence_quote: Sum 7 is the most likely at 16.67%, and it's exactly 6× more likely than sum 2 at 2.78%
claims.reasoning: Peak, values, and 6x ratio all match source exactly.

claims.claim_text: Sums 2-12 have 1-2-3-4-5-6-5-4-3-2-1 ways of 36; 1 way versus 6 ordered ways.
claims.evidence_quote: For sum 2, there's only one way ... sum 7 ... order matters, so that's 6 ways total out of 36
claims.reasoning: Way counts mirror the source table and proof.

claims.claim_text: Column 7 is only about 4.3x longer (13/3) than column 2, not 6x.
claims.evidence_quote: it's only 13/3 ≈ 4.3× longer
claims.reasoning: Source states the 4.3x figure via 13/3.

claims.claim_text: Four-dice pairing offers three pairings and sharply flattens the distribution.
claims.evidence_quote: That's it, just three possible pairings ... Did the distribution get flatter?
claims.reasoning: Source confirms three pairings and a flatter distribution.

claims.claim_text: P(can make 2) = 171/1296 approx 13.2%, up from two-dice 2.78%.
claims.reasoning: Fraction and percentage match source.

claims.claim_text: P(can make 7) = 834/1296 approx 64.4% via inclusion-exclusion; overlaps 24/1296, triple 0.
claims.reasoning: All four numbers match source inclusion-exclusion result.

claims.claim_text: Full range 13.2% to 64.4%; probability ratio 4.88 nearly matches length ratio 4.33.
claims.evidence_quote: The probability ratio from 2 to 7 is 4.88. The length ratio is 4.33
claims.reasoning: Both ratios and endpoints match source table.

claims.claim_text: Three-column combination choice dominates single-column odds.
claims.evidence_quote: column combination choice dominates individual column balance
claims.reasoning: Source states combination choice dominates individual columns.

claims.claim_text: Expected rolls L/P: column 2 needs 22.73, column 7 needs 20.18 rolls.

claims.reasoning: Expected-roll values match source table.

claims.claim_text: {6,7,8} succeeds 1193/1296 = 92.0% with Q 1.43 markers per roll.

claims.claim_text: {2,3,12} succeeds only 568/1296 = 43.8% with Q 1.05; bust likelier.

claims.claim_text: All 165 combos ranked; 37 excellent at 85%+, median 79.6%, worst 43.8%.

claims.reasoning: Counts and percentages match source distribution summary.

claims.claim_text: Clean moves only: 39.8% for {6,7,8} and 2.3% for {2,3,12}.

claims.reasoning: Both clean-move percentages match source.

claims.claim_text: Keep rolling while expected gain exceeds expected loss.

claims.reasoning: Source states the same expected-gain heuristic.

claims.claim_text: Rule: continue if (P_success x Q) > (P_bust x U); {6,7,8} gives 1.32 > 0.4.
claims.reasoning: Formula and worked values match source.

claims.claim_text: {2,3,12} with 2 steps gives 1.12 > 0.46 loss, so stop.
claims.evidence_quote: Risk: 0.562 × 2 = 1.12 steps ... Expected gain: 0.438 × 1.05 = 0.46 steps ... you should STOP
claims.reasoning: Source computes the same figures and conclusion.

claims.claim_text: Continuation usually beats switching, but full quantitative comparison remains open future work.
claims.evidence_quote: The mathematics favor continuation in most cases ... I haven't fully analyzed this aspect quantitatively ... open question for future work
